look_here_first: DALLISGRASS: on ONE complete seedhead count about 3–7(11) laterally spreading one-sided racemes. Its mature spikelets are generally 3–4 mm, broadly ovate and conspicuously LONG-SILKY-HAIRED at the upper-glume margins. Compare with vaseygrass: often 10–20 racemes and smaller 2–3 mm spikelets; these counts overlap. Existing Joey photos show the true racemes and leaf collar area, NOT measured ligules or the decisive silky margins.

crew_field_steps: See the mature inflorescence as a whole: several slender arching racemes attached at different heights on a central flowering axis.
At the leaf blade/sheathed stem junction, the existing Joey photograph visibly shows a blade-base and pale collar hair area, but no independently measured membranous ligule.
For species confirmation, magnify a full mature flattened spikelet, its margin hairs and a ruler; counts/height alone overlap P. urvillei.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Entire flowering culm with lower branches and count on ONE head.
Single complete branch at scale showing rows of spikelets and attachment.
Several mature spikelets in side/face view under 10–20×, ruler beside 3–4 mm units and long edge hairs.
Leaf collar membrane and sheath mouth (correct part clearly exposed); compare vaseygrass.
Rooted tuft size and basal sheaths.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Measure 5 mature spikelets from the same head at 10–20×, showing edges backlit against a 1-mm ruler. Counts/height overlap P. urvillei. Paired spikelets are on a one-sided raceme, not awns. The pale hair tuft near blade/sheath in the Joey photo must not be labelled as a measured membranous ligule.
do_not_use_alone: Number of racemes without the entire flowering axis
Habitat, height, or vegetative tuft in isolation
Microscopic glume hairs or spikelet length inferred from a photo without scale
comparisons.field_identification_note: Photograph entire panicle with all raceme attachment points on SAME culm; follow one raceme from its base. On 5 detached mature 3–4 mm spikelets record true silky marginal hairs and upper-glume outline. Leaf collar photo is a site-reference only.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Paspalum: what to inspect
steps: NEW REAL ANATOMY: source-author photos in gallery panels 7–9 (indices 6–8) show actual 5mm scale and three sets of hairy green oval attached spikelets in front/reverse. The dark feathery tufts are true flower stigmas, NOT awns; source photos do not individually assign upper glume/lemma.

Start with the original whole flowering-head photograph (panel 1), then the TWO PHYSICALLY ARCHIVED AND PIXEL-VERIFIED source-identified anatomy photographs: blade/sheath membranous ligule and collar hairs (panel 5) and hairy attached spikelets (panel 6). Five new arrows point only to visible structures and the original 10-mm scale; no independent measurement of the ligule or dissected spikelet.
First show the WHOLE head, then ONE one-sided raceme and attached spikelets. Never treat a photograph of one branch as total raceme count.
Obtain a real intact mature spikelet and measure it with 1-mm reference; use margin hair pattern and glumes to separate close Paspalum taxa.
Photograph blade/sheath joint and same-plant rootstock; knotgrass needs actually rooted horizontal stolons, not merely a low mat.
If plant photo is source-labelled only, keep identity tentative and leave existing county-native fields unchanged.

NEW exact distinct species comparisons: panel 10 is Harry Rose P. urvillei mature spikelet with photographer's ORIGINAL glume/lemma labels; panel 11 is David Stang P. floridanum 2-raceme head. Do not transfer organs or assumed Hays locality/native status between species.

Bahia grass generally has two terminal racemes and lacks the distinct long marginal silky fringe characteristic of dallisgrass.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.details: On ONE complete flowering culm, follow each branch from its attachment on the main axis. Dallisgrass is a coarse perennial with spreading to drooping racemes and paired overlapping spikelets in rows on the underside. Existing panel 0 teaches the branching habit but overlapping plants prevent a reliable total count. Branch count alone does NOT separate vaseygrass. New exact photographic reproductive views in gallery panels 7–9 (indices6–8) show attached rows and 5-mm scale, but still cannot establish total racemes on one full flowering head; whole flowering culm remains priority. Do not count several separate overlapping plants as one head.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE HEAD; WHOLE SAME-PLANT PANICLE GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE ROOTED TUFT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial clump with short rhizomes, not long stolons
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published Williamson County plants have a fibrous-rooted perennial tuft and short rhizomes with nodal roots; basal sheaths can be hairy. A complete same-plant root-to-head photograph with centimeter scale is missing. Do not infer underground rhizomes from the existing detached flowering-head panels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED GROWTH FORM; ROOTED CROWN PHOTO GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Membranous ligule 2–5.5 mm in local treatment
field_id_short_tiles.details: Open the INNER blade–sheath junction. The Williamson County treatment describes a translucent membranous ligule about 2–5.5 mm; broader GrassBase accounts allow 2–8 mm. The physically archived Stefan.lefnaer source-identified CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph in gallery panel 5 (index 4) now visibly shows a translucent ligule flap, adjacent fine collar hairs and the photographer's 10-mm reference; three gross-structure arrows were separately pixel-reviewed. This is genuine anatomy evidence, but the free apex and exact membrane length were NOT independently measured, and the specimen is Croatian, not a Hays voucher. Joey panels 2–3 (indices 1–2) show external collar context only; never measure those hairs as the membrane.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE LIGULE FLAP PHOTOGRAPHED — CALIBRATED FREE APEX AND LOCAL VOUCHER MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Typically 3–4 mm; paired and broadly ovate
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find five ripe spikelets on one one-sided raceme and photograph flat and convex faces beside a physical 1-mm ruler at 10–20×. Williamson County reports upper glumes about 3.5–3.7 × 2.2–2.4 mm; broader GrassBase spikelet range is about 2.7–3.9 mm. Physically archived Harry Rose gallery panel 6 (index 5) visibly demonstrates oval attached spikelets and silky marginal hairs, with two pixel-reviewed gross arrows. It has NO calibrated ruler, so neither exact length nor a particular glume/lemma boundary is established. NEW Stefan CC BY-SA4 panels 7–9 now give actual 5-mm scale with enlarged attached oval spikelets, and an eight-faced view; distinctive pale marginal hairs are genuinely pictured. Still not separately isolated upper glume / lower sterile lemma or definite 3.5–3.7 mm individual measurement unless scale is calibrated in same plane.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE SILKY SPIKELETS PHOTOGRAPHED — MATURE MILLIMETER MEASUREMENT MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE SILKY UPPER GLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume absent; upper glume silky-edged; awnless
field_id_short_tiles.details: A true LOWER GLUME is absent. In the Williamson County treatment, the upper glume is spikelet-length, about 3.5–3.7 mm and 5–7-veined (broader treatments 3–9); the lower sterile lemma is near glume-length and the hard glossy upper fertile lemma about 2.2 mm locally (2–3.2 mm broadly). There is no long lemma awn: silky marginal glume hairs are not awns. Gallery panel 6 (index 5) now actually resolves silky hairs along attached oval spikelets, but does NOT distinguish their origin on the upper glume from overlapping bract edges. A ripe, forceps-separated and scaled spikelet is still required before glume, lemma, palea or vein arrows. NEW photos 7–9 visually establish true silky marginal hairs, some dark feathery STIGMAS (not awns) and close oval spikelet shape. Vaseygrass OTHER species gallery panel 10 has its photographer's own accurate glume/lemma labels; they CANNOT be re-used to prove Dallisgrass dissection. Actual upper glume/sterile lemma origin still needs dedicated dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SILKY MARGINS VISIBLE — GLUME/LEMMA ORIGIN AND VEINS NEED DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE VASEYGRASS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Dallisgrass usually fewer racemes and larger silky spikelets
field_id_short_tiles.details: Paspalum urvillei commonly has more slender racemes (often 10–20) and smaller ripe spikelets (~2–3 mm), but head counts and spikelet sizes can overlap. Panel 3 is explicitly a DIFFERENT-SPECIES vaseygrass reference, not a Dallisgrass image. Compare equally mature, ruler-scaled spikelets, upper-glume hair placement, and a whole head from each species; avoid using wet habitat or clump size alone. NEW comparison panel 10 (index9) is a true locally archived vaseygrass original annotated glume/lemma; panel 11 (index10) is a true source-authenticated native Florida paspalum head with two branches. Both clearly labelled different species. Do not copy their organ labels to Dallisgrass and do not infer Florida paspalum Hays BONAP nativity status from non-Hays imagery.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TWO VERIFIED VASEY/NATIVE FLORIDA PHOTO COMPARISONS NOW INCLUDED — SAME-SCALE SPIKELET DETAILS STILL OPEN
